title: Try /review
body: Use /review when you want AI review comments on the PR.

title: Try /fix
body: Use /fix when you want to apply a /review's findings, or named suggestions.

title: Try /switch
body: Use /switch when you want future PR work to use a different model.

title: Try /use
body: Use /use when you want one immediate follow-up run with a temporary model.

title: Try /ultrafix
body: Use /ultrafix when you want an automated review-fix loop.

title: Try /merge
body: Use /merge when you want the base branch merged into the PR branch.

title: Choose how to launch a goal
body: Goals support two launch strategies: Agent implements directly opens a draft PR and commits changes at checkpoints; Agent orchestrates through ProPR lets the agent decompose work, create issues, and start and monitor their implementation. Use Goals for an ongoing objective and Planner Studio when you want to inspect and refine a plan before running it.

title: Plan before implementation
body: ProPR is designed to put structure in front of agent runs. Instead of sending a vague issue straight to a coding agent, use Planner Studio to create a draft, gather context, review the plan, refine it, and approve the work when it is ready.

title: Keep repository to-dos
body: The To-Dos tab turns ongoing maintenance ideas into trackable work. Todos are organized into categories, can be reordered by drag-and-drop, searched, edited, completed, and restored after completion.

title: Tune repository indexing
body: Summarization runs through a configurable agent and model, with an optional fallback model and quota-aware retry: when the primary model hits a provider quota, ProPR records a cooldown and switches to the fallback so indexing keeps progressing instead of failing.

title: Choose agents and models per phase
body: ProPR runs coding work through configurable agents. Each agent is a CLI tool packaged in its own Docker image, with an isolated credential directory mounted into that image. Models are addressed by stable ProPR model IDs that work everywhere a model can be chosen: issue labels, the Web UI, the CLI (-a/-m), and PR commands (/switch, /use, /review <model>).

title: Monitor provider usage with Agent Tank
body: Agent Tank is a separate, optional local tool that monitors the usage limits of your AI coding agent CLIs. ProPR integrates with it to show live provider capacity in the Web UI and to record per-call usage deltas alongside every LLM log entry.

title: Keep track of work in your inbox
body: The Show an unread-count badge on the installed app preference asks the browser's Badging API to show the Inbox unread count, capped at 99. Push receipt and foreground Inbox refresh both update it; reading or dismissing notifications reduces or clears it.

title: Connect tools through MCP
body: This is the flow the operator surface is built for: find out what is happening, drill into one piece of work, act on its pull request, and check afterwards what the connected app actually did.
